authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
jurisdiction: United States (extraterritorial via Foreign Direct Product rules)
name: EAR: Implementation of additional export controls on certain advanced computing and semiconductor manufacturing items (87 FR 62186)
requirements: Licence requirements for advanced computing ICs (new 3A090, 4A090; 600 GB/s and TPP 4800) and SME (new 3B090) for China; fab end-use control for logic 16/14 nm or non-planar, DRAM 18 nm half-pitch, NAND 128+ layers; US-persons licence requirement (744.6(c)(2)) with presumption of denial except US/A:5/A:6-headquartered end users; two new FDP rules (advanced computing, supercomputer); footnote 4 for 28 Chinese Entity List entities [CLM-0301, CLM-0302, CLM-0303]. Effective in two steps, 7 and 21 October 2022. Amended by 88 FR 73424/73458 (Oct 2023), 89 FR 23876 (Apr 2024), 89 FR 96790 (Dec 2024).

authority: US Congress; US Department of Commerce (CHIPS Program Office)
name: CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 - CHIPS for America manufacturing incentives and R&D
requirements: USD 52.7bn over five years for Commerce semiconductor programmes [CLM-0311], of which USD 39bn manufacturing incentives and USD 11bn R&D [CLM-0312]; plus up to USD 75bn loan authority backed by USD 6bn of the 39bn [@oig_total, @gao_loansub]; eligible 'covered entities' include fabrication, assembly, test, advanced packaging, materials and equipment facilities [CLM-0024]; awards move from nonbinding PMT to final direct funding agreement and are disbursed as reimbursements on verified milestones, with clawbacks [@oig_pmt, @gao_reimburse]. First NOFO: direct funding generally 5-15% of capex, total incl. loans up to 35%, max USD 3bn per project without extra certification [@gao_nofo_range]; upside sharing required above USD 150m [@gao_upside_rule]; childcare requirements removed by 2025-26 amendments [@gao_amend14]; dividend and buyback limits (e.g. Micron) [@mu_conditions]. Status: 19 companies / 40 projects, USD 30.9bn direct funding + USD 5.5bn loans awarded by July 2025 [@gao_awards]; USD 6bn disbursed by July 2025 [@gao_disbursed] plus USD 5.695bn accelerated to Intel in Aug 2025 in exchange for equity [@intc_close]; 12 PMTs incl. Wolfspeed USD 750m still unfinalised June 2026 [@crs_pending]; no awards publicly rescinded as of July 2026 [@crs_norescind]; 14 awards amended Jan 2025-Apr 2026 [@gao_amend14]. R&D: USD 7.8bn of USD 11bn in awards cancelled (Natcast NSTC, SRC SMART USA, NAPMP), USD 506.8m expended; replaced by an equity-seeking BAA [@gao_rd_cancel, @gao_rd_spent, @baa_equity]. After March 2025 the CPO sits under the US Investment Accelerator [CLM-0316, @oig_accel]. FY2026 is the last year of advance appropriations for incentives [@crs_fy26].

authority: European Parliament and Council; European Commission
name: European Chips Act - Regulation (EU) 2023/1781
requirements: Three pillars: Chips for Europe Initiative, security of supply (first-of-a-kind facilities, State aid) and monitoring/crisis response [CLM-0327, CLM-0328]; 18 State aid decisions over EUR 32bn of investment approved [CLM-0329]; expected to mobilise more than EUR 43bn public investment, 20% share target by 2030 [CLM-0141].

authority: Wassenaar Arrangement (42 participating states)
name: Wassenaar Arrangement List of Dual-Use Goods and Technologies
requirements: Common dual-use control list, decided by consensus and implemented through each participating state's national law [CLM-0342]; flows into EU law [CLM-0343].

authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) with General Administration of Customs
name: China export licensing of gallium and germanium items
requirements: Exports of gallium and germanium items require licences from 1 Aug 2023 [CLM-0344]; China produced ~60% of germanium and ~90% of gallium in 2022 [CLM-0345].

authority: Ministry of Electronics and IT / India Semiconductor Mission
name: Semicon India programme (India Semiconductor Mission)
requirements: Rs 76,000 crore framework with up to 50% fiscal support for silicon fabs, compound-semiconductor facilities, assembly/test units and chip design [CLM-0358]; 10 projects worth Rs 1.60 lakh crore approved by Dec 2025 [CLM-0359].

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
name: EAR: Foreign-Produced Direct Product Rule additions and refinements to controls for advanced computing and semiconductor manufacturing items (89 FR 96790)
requirements: New FDP rules for SME (Macau/D:5) and footnote 5 entities, zero de minimis for specified SME containing US ICs, 24 SME types and 3 software tools, HBM controls (3A090.c, >2 GB/s/mm2), ECAD/TCAD and software-key controls, eight new red flags, DRAM advanced-node criteria changed [CLM-0304]. Allied exclusion via Supp. 4 to Part 742 (33 countries; not Korea or Taiwan). Effective 2 Dec 2024, compliance 31 Dec 2024 for certain controls. FDP and de minimis provisions still in eCFR as of 2026-09-01.

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
name: EAR Entity List 'affiliates rule' (50% ownership; 90 FR 47201) and its one-year suspension
requirements: Entities at least 50% owned by Entity List parties automatically inherit Entity List restrictions [CLM-0305]. Suspended 10 Nov 2025 to 9 Nov 2026, to be reinstated automatically unless further action [CLM-0306]. Status field 'unknown' because the schema has no 'suspended' value.

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
name: BIS revision to licence review policy for advanced computing commodities (H200-class chips to China and Macau)
requirements: Licence review for H200-class and less-advanced AI chips to China/Macau moved from presumption of denial to case-by-case, with conditions incl. independent third-party testing in the US and no reduction of capacity available to US customers [CLM-0307, CLM-0308].

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
name: AI Diffusion Rule (January 2025) and its announced rescission
requirements: AI Diffusion IFR 90 FR 4544 (published 15 Jan 2025, effective 13 Jan 2025). BIS announced on 13 May 2025 it would not enforce and would formally rescind it (compliance date 15 May 2025), and issued guidance on Huawei Ascend chips and AI-chip diversion [CLM-0309, CLM-0310]. No rescission rule found in the Federal Register BIS rule list through 30 Sep 2026; a law-firm review (Aug 2026) says it remains in the CFR but unenforced.

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
name: Export controls on ECAD software for GAAFET integrated circuits (87 FR 49979, August 2022; ECCN 3D006)
requirements: Controls on ECAD software specially designed for developing GAAFET ICs (new ECCN 3D006), part of an IFR implementing December 2021 Wassenaar decisions on four Section 1758 technologies [CLM-0409]. The rule was effective 15 Aug 2022 but ECCN 3D006 only from 14 Oct 2022; NS and AT licence requirements per Country Chart. BIS described GAAFET as key to 3 nm and below [CLM-0408]. Extended December 2024 by ECAD/TCAD controls for advanced-node ICs produced in Macau/D:5. Current status not re-checked.

authority: US Department of Commerce / BIS
name: Entity List designation of Huawei Technologies and 68 non-US affiliates (84 FR 22961, May 2019)
requirements: Licence required for all items subject to the EAR, presumption of denial; Huawei plus 68 non-US affiliates in 26 destinations; 38 more affiliates added August 2020. Announced 15 May 2019 [CLM-0135]. Extended by the Huawei FDP rules (2020). Current listing status not re-checked.

authority: US Department of Commerce (NIST)
name: CHIPS 'guardrails': Preventing the improper use of CHIPS Act funding (15 CFR Part 231)
penalties: Expansion clawback: recovery of up to the full award if a recipient materially expands (more than 5% of capacity via added cleanroom, line or space) semiconductor capacity in a foreign country of concern within 10 years; existing legacy facilities may expand 10% over 10 years [@gr_material]. Technology clawback: full award recovered for knowing joint research or technology licensing with a foreign entity of concern on national-security-relevant technology [@gr_tech]. Parallel 48D recapture of 100% of credits [@recapture]. No post-2023 amendment found [@gr_nochange].
requirements: For ten years CHIPS recipients may not materially expand semiconductor capacity in a foreign country of concern, and joint research/technology licensing with foreign entities of concern is restricted [CLM-0313]; defines legacy nodes (28 nm logic, DRAM >18 nm half-pitch, NAND <128 layers) [CLM-0028].

authority: US Congress; Internal Revenue Service (Treasury)
name: Advanced manufacturing investment credit (26 U.S.C. 48D)
requirements: Investment tax credit for facilities whose primary purpose is making semiconductors or semiconductor manufacturing equipment; 35% for property placed in service after 2025 (25% before) following P.L. 119-21 [CLM-0278, CLM-0315, @irs_rates]; qualified property is tangible depreciable property integral to the facility, excluding office/administrative buildings [@irs_bldg]; no credit for construction beginning after 31 Dec 2026 [CLM-0280, @crs_itc_deadline], construction start shown by physical work or 5% safe harbor [@boc]; elective (direct) payment with IRS pre-filing registration [CLM-0281, @irs_reg]; 10-year recapture for material expansion in a foreign country of concern [@recapture]. Scored at USD 24.3bn over 2022-2031 at enactment [@cbo_48d]; no official estimate of the 35% increase found [@cost35_unknown]. NIST's fact sheet and some filings still say 25% (CON-0009) [CLM-0367, @tsmc_25itc]. Industry seeks extension beyond 2026 [@semi_ext]; none enacted as of Sept 2026 [@ext_unknown].

authority: President of the United States (Section 232)
name: Section 232 proclamation: Adjusting imports of semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and their derivative products
requirements: 25% ad valorem duty on certain advanced computing chips and derivative products [CLM-0319], with exemptions for US data centres, repairs, R&D, startups, non-data-centre consumer and civil industrial uses and US public-sector use [CLM-0320]; broader tariffs may follow; market review required by 1 July 2026 [CLM-0321]. Phase two signalled but not published as of 3 Sept 2026 (tier-3) [CLM-0322].

authority: Office of the US Trade Representative
name: Section 301 action on China's targeting of the semiconductor industry
requirements: Additional tariff on Chinese semiconductors (18 tariff lines incl. wafers, transistors, diodes, ICs) at 0% from 23 Dec 2025, rising on 23 Jun 2027 to a rate to be announced, on top of an existing 50% Section 301 tariff [CLM-0323, CLM-0324].

authority: US Department of the Treasury
name: Outbound Investment Security Program
requirements: Prohibits or requires notification of certain investments by US persons in Chinese (incl. Hong Kong, Macau) entities active in semiconductors and microelectronics, quantum and AI [CLM-0325].

authority: US Securities and Exchange Commission
name: SEC conflict minerals disclosure (Form SD)
requirements: SEC-reporting companies using tin, tantalum, tungsten or gold necessary to their products file an annual Form SD by 31 May on DRC-region origin [CLM-0326]. Which chip participant types file is an interpretation.

authority: US Department of Defense - Defense Microelectronics Activity
name: DMEA Trusted Supplier Program (accreditation)
requirements: Accredits trusted suppliers in IC design, aggregation, brokering, mask manufacturing, foundry, post-processing, packaging/assembly and test, to assure integrity and confidentiality of ICs [CLM-0458, CLM-0459]. Voluntary for suppliers; relevant to defence work.

authority: European Commission
name: European Chips Act 2.0 (proposal)
requirements: Proposed 3 June 2026 to boost the chips industry, reduce strategic dependencies and support advanced production; not adopted as of sources read [CLM-0330]; priorities reported by SEMI include expanding first-of-a-kind, permitting and demand stimulation [CLM-0331].

authority: European Commission (DG Trade)
name: EU dual-use Regulation (EU) 2021/821 - 2026 update of Annex I control list
requirements: Adds EU-level controls on certain semiconductor manufacturing and testing equipment and materials and on advanced computing ICs; enters into force on publication after a two-month scrutiny period [CLM-0332]; aligned with Wassenaar decisions [CLM-0343]. Status 'proposed' = in scrutiny as of Sept 2026.

authority: Council of the EU and European Parliament
name: Revised EU foreign direct investment screening regulation
requirements: Provisional agreement (Dec 2025) requiring all member states to screen foreign investment in sensitive areas incl. semiconductors, applying 18 months after entry into force [CLM-0333]. Entry into force not confirmed.

authority: European Parliament and Council
name: EU F-gas Regulation (EU) 2024/573
requirements: Regulates fluorinated greenhouse gases; whether and how it treats gases used in semiconductor manufacturing could not be confirmed [CLM-0334].

authority: European Chemicals Agency / European Commission
name: EU universal PFAS restriction under REACH
requirements: Status and treatment of semiconductor manufacturing uses not established [CLM-0335].

authority: Netherlands Minister for Foreign Trade and Development
name: Netherlands national export licence requirement for advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment
requirements: National export authorisation for advanced SME starting with DUV lithography (1 Sept 2023) [CLM-0336]; extended 7 Sept 2024 [CLM-0337, CLM-0140]; metrology and inspection equipment added 1 Apr 2025 [CLM-0338].

authority: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (Japan)
name: Japan export controls on 23 types of semiconductor manufacturing equipment (Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act)
requirements: 23 SME types added to export controls for all destinations in July 2023 [CLM-0339].

authority: Government of Japan / METI
name: Japan AI and semiconductor public support framework (JPY 10 trillion+ by FY2030)
requirements: Government stated in Nov 2024 it would provide public support of JPY 10tn or more to AI and semiconductors by FY2030 [CLM-0340]; Rapidus selected under the information-processing promotion law with JPY 100bn IPA investment (company's own report) [CLM-0341]. Legal instruments and amounts by recipient not established.

authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
name: MOFCOM Notice 2024 No. 46 (dual-use export ban to US military users; US-specific Ga/Ge/Sb/superhard ban)
requirements: Bans dual-use exports to US military users and in principle prohibits gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials exports to the US [CLM-0346]; the US-specific prohibition is suspended until 27 Nov 2026 [CLM-0347] (tier-3 source for the suspension).

authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
name: MOFCOM Notice 2025 No. 61 (rare-earth 0.1% de minimis rule)
requirements: Would require Chinese export permits for foreign-made items containing Chinese-origin rare earths worth 0.1% or more of value [CLM-0348]; suspended 7 Nov 2025 to 10 Nov 2026 via Announcement No. 70 [CLM-0349] (tier-3 source for the suspension).

authority: Ministry of Finance and 19 state-owned investors
name: China National IC Industry Investment Fund Phase III (Big Fund III)
requirements: Registered May 2024 with CNY 344bn capital [CLM-0350]; earlier phases CNY 138.7bn (2014) and 204bn (2019) [CLM-0132]. Investees and terms not researched.

authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
name: China anti-dumping investigation into US analog ICs (September 2025)
requirements: Investigation into certain US interface and gate-driver analog ICs, plus an anti-discrimination probe into US chip measures [CLM-0351]; outcome unknown [CLM-0352].

authority: Cybersecurity Review Office (CAC)
name: China Cybersecurity Review Office decision on Micron products (May 2023)
requirements: Critical information infrastructure operators required to stop purchasing Micron products after a security review [CLM-0353]. Tier-3 source only.

authority: National Assembly / Ministry of Economy and Finance (Korea)
name: South Korea Restriction of Special Taxation Act amendment ('K-Chips Act', February 2025)
requirements: Facility-investment tax credit for semiconductors raised to 20% for large companies and 30% for SMEs [CLM-0354]. Tier-3 source only; legal text not read.

authority: National Assembly (Korea)
name: South Korea Special Act on Strengthening and Supporting the Competitiveness of the Semiconductor Industry
requirements: Passed 29 Jan 2026 without the 52-hour workweek exemption; expected to take effect Q3 2026, entry into force not confirmed [CLM-0355]. Tier-3 source only.

authority: Legislative Yuan / Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan)
name: Taiwan Statute for Industrial Innovation, Article 10-2 ('Taiwan Chips Act')
requirements: 25% tax credit on R&D and 5% on advanced-process equipment for firms meeting thresholds (NT$6bn R&D, 6% R&D intensity, 12%/15% effective tax rate); applications from Feb 2024 [CLM-0356]. Tier-2 source; statute text not read.

authority: MOEA International Trade Administration (Taiwan)
name: Taiwan Strategic High-Tech Commodities entity list (June 2025 additions incl. Huawei and SMIC)
requirements: 601 entities incl. Huawei and SMIC added to the export-control entity list [CLM-0357]. Tier-2 source; affected types are an interpretation (Taiwanese exporters).

authority: Ministry of Electronics and IT / India Semiconductor Mission
name: India Semiconductor Mission 2.0
requirements: Announced in Union Budget 2026-27, focused on equipment, materials, Indian semiconductor IP and supply chains, with Rs 1,000 crore for FY2026-27 [CLM-0360]. Operational status not established.

authority: SEMI International Standards Program
name: SEMI International Standards (e.g. E30 GEM, E142, P39 OASIS)
requirements: Voluntary consensus standards on equipment automation, facilities, gases, materials, lithography, packaging, chemicals, silicon and traceability [CLM-0361, CLM-0362]; E30 defines equipment-to-host communication [CLM-0453]; E142 wafer/substrate maps [CLM-0454].

authority: JEDEC Solid State Technology Association
name: JEDEC memory and packaging standards (incl. HBM4, JESD270-4)
requirements: Open standards for DDR, LPDDR, HBM, flash, packaging and ESD [CLM-0363]; HBM4 released 16 Apr 2025 [CLM-0440].

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
name: EAR: Huawei entity-specific foreign-produced direct product rule (85 FR 29849, May 2020; broadened by 85 FR 51596, August 2020)
requirements: Foreign-made items that are direct products of US software/technology, or made in plants that are direct products of US technology, need a licence when destined to Huawei 'footnote 1' entities; transition to 14 Sep 2020 for items in production before 15 May 2020. August 2020 revision extended scope to Huawei as purchaser, consignee or end-user and to items incorporated into Huawei products, Categories 3-5. Footnote 1 FDP still listed in 15 CFR 734.9(e) as of Sept 2026.

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
name: Entity List designation of SMIC and related entities (85 FR 83416, December 2020)
requirements: SMIC and 10 related entities listed; presumption of denial for items uniquely required for 10 nm and below (incl. EUV), case-by-case otherwise; reason: military-civil fusion. Later modifications to SMIC entries (e.g. December 2024 modifications of 14 Chinese entries) not individually checked.

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
name: EAR: Export Controls on Semiconductor Manufacturing Items (88 FR 73424, October 2023)
requirements: Controls on more SME types and licence requirements extended beyond China and Macau to 21 arms-embargoed countries. Corrected April 2024 and expanded December 2024 (REG-0007).

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
jurisdiction: United States (extraterritorial via advanced computing FDP)
name: EAR: Advanced Computing Items; Supercomputer and Semiconductor End Use; Updates and Corrections (88 FR 73458, October 2023)
requirements: Replaced interconnect-bandwidth test with TPP and performance density; scope broadened to D:1, D:4, D:5 not in A:5/A:6 and 40+ countries; License Exception NAC with 25-day review. Amended by 89 FR 23876, 90 FR 4544, 90 FR 5298 and 91 FR 1684.

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
name: EAR: Commerce Control List Additions and Revisions; Implementation of Controls on Advanced Technologies Consistent With Controls Implemented by International Partners (89 FR 72926, September 2024)
requirements: New ECCNs incl. certain etch tools, EUV masks, SEM tools, cryogenic CMOS and GAAFET technology; License Exception IEC for countries with equivalent controls; worldwide NS/RS licence requirements with approval presumption for A:1 and denial for D:1/D:5. Later changes not checked.
short_name: Sept 2024 plurilateral controls / License Exception IEC

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
jurisdiction: United States (applies to foundries and OSATs worldwide handling EAR-subject ICs)
name: EAR: Implementation of Additional Due Diligence Measures for Advanced Computing Integrated Circuits (90 FR 5298, January 2025) - foundry/OSAT due-diligence rule
requirements: Presumption that 16/14 nm-or-below logic ICs are 3A090.a unless approved/authorised designer, transistor-count safe harbour (30bn; 35bn 2027; 40bn 2029) without HBM, or approved OSAT attestation; approved IC designer and approved OSAT lists; KYC and quarterly reporting for authorised designers. Authorised-designer status and approval-application deadline extended to 31 Dec 2026 by 91 FR 17851.

authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security
name: EAR: Revocation of Validated End-User Authorizations in the PRC (90 FR 42321, September 2025)
requirements: Removes Samsung China Semiconductor, SK hynix Semiconductor (China) and Intel Semiconductor (Dalian) from VEU; suppliers now need individual licences (~1,000 extra applications/yr); BIS intends to license operation of existing fabs but not capacity expansion or technology upgrades. TSMC Nanjing VEU revocation reported but not seen in FR.

authority: US Department of the Treasury; Internal Revenue Service
name: Advanced manufacturing investment credit final regulations (T.D. 10009)
penalties: Recapture of 100% of previously allowed 48D credits for applicable transactions within 10 years [@recapture].
requirements: Implements 26 USC 48D: beginning-of-construction via physical work test or 5% safe harbor with continuity requirement [@boc]; 10-year recapture of 100% of credits if an applicable taxpayer materially expands semiconductor capacity in a foreign country of concern [@recapture]. Elective payment rules finalised separately (T.D. 9989).

authority: NIST CHIPS Research and Development Office
name: CHIPS R&D Office Broad Agency Announcement 2025-NIST-CHIPS-CRDO-01
requirements: Rolling solicitation (white paper then full proposal) through September 2029 for research, prototyping and commercial solutions in microelectronics; awards as other transaction agreements; applicants may be required to give Commerce equity, warrants, IP licences, royalties or revenue sharing [@baa, @baa_equity]. Described as the primary mechanism for CHIPS R&D awards [@baa_primary]; first awards (xLight, SandboxAQ, I-Pulse; US$900m) include equity for Commerce [@gao_newawards].

authority: US Department of Commerce, International Trade Administration
name: Countervailing duty order: DRAMs from the Republic of Korea (C-580-851; 68 FR 47546)
requirements: Cash deposits of 44.29% on DRAMs and DRAM modules from Hynix and all other Korean producers except Samsung (de minimis subsidies, excluded), after Commerce found Korean government-directed creditor support to Hynix and the ITC found material injury (4 Aug 2003). Later status (revocation) not verified in this run.
short_name: 2003 US CVD order on Korean DRAMs (Hynix)

authority: Governments of the United States and Japan
name: US-Japan Semiconductor Arrangement (1986)
requirements: Japan to facilitate foreign market access and prevent dumping in the US and third markets [CLM-0099]; MITI implemented it by cutting output/exports to hit price targets, raising DRAM prices (Irwin p. 11). Third-market provision ended 1988 after a GATT panel; US dumping provision ended with the 1991 renegotiated agreement (Irwin pp. 11-12).
